verdict_rows: | w373 `CLAIMS.jsonl`, `S1.w373.001` | KEEP | Same line 551 contains no current-open certification and no hypotheses. | Source-scope verdict only. |

| w373 `INDEPENDENT.md`, rare-event family | KEEP | Recompute `Var(X_n)=(1-1/n)n^(2/3)+n^(1/3)` and the lower bound `n^(-1)exp(alpha n^(2/3-a))`; threshold is `a=2/3`. | Abstract random-variable counterexample, not iid FPP. It defeats an inference from variance scaling alone; it does not defeat an FPP-specific argument. |

| w372 `S1.w372.L1-short`; w373 small-endpoint obstruction | KEEP | Direct edge cost at most 2, every alternative simple path has at least 3 edges and cost at least 3. For `2e_1`, direct cost is strictly below 4 almost surely, every detour costs at least 4. | Refutes an all-nonzero-endpoint positive wandering lower bound for Uniform[1,2], while Chatterjee (A4) excludes a finite neighborhood. |

| w372 `S1.w372.L2` | KEEP | Put `r=sd G_i`. Centering gives `|r-s|<=delta`. Since both errors are nonnegative, `||Delta_1-Delta_2||_2^2<=2delta^2`. Independence of `G_1,G_2` gives `||G_1-G_2||_2=sqrt(2)r`; both triangle inequalities yield the stated `2(s±2delta)^2` bounds. | No independence of unrestricted passage times or conditioned geodesics is used. Application still needs `delta/s -> 0`. |

| w372 `S1.w372.CEX`; w373 high-probability agreement example | KEEP | For the common-shock example `Var F_i=n^(2b)(1-p_n)` but `F_1-F_2=0`. For w373's example, agreement probability is `1-1/n` while variance changes from 0 to `n-1`. | Both are abstract counterexamples to an inference, not FPP counterexamples. |

| w372 `S1.w372.L4` | KEEP conditional | For an off-cylinder geodesic vertex `z`, additivity gives `H_n <= |T(0,z)-m(z)|+|T(z,v)-m(v-z)|+|T(0,v)-m(v)|`. Apply exponential Markov to each fixed `z`; the `l1` ball has at most `(4n+1)^d` vertices. | Requires an unproved uniform positive mean gap `H_n`; it does not imply global exponent matching. |

| w373 `ATTEMPT.md`, geodesic-selection example | KEEP | For two independent continuous path costs with common median `m`, on `E={A<B}`, `P(A<=m|E)=P(B>=m|E)=3/4`, while `P(A<=m,B>=m|E)=1/2`; the false product is `9/16`, error `1/16`. | Finite square graph only. It warns against conditioning, not against w372's unconditional deterministic-cylinder independence. |
